finalText:
I've finished the research. Some planned sources returned 404 (the spec's `parsing.html` page and javascript.info), so the answer relies on the WHATWG scripting section, MDN and web.dev. Where they differ, I treat the WHATWG spec as normative.

## Short answer

With no attributes, a classic script stops the HTML parser until it has downloaded and run. `defer` downloads in parallel and runs the scripts in document order after parsing ends, before `DOMContentLoaded`. `async` downloads in parallel and runs each script as soon as it arrives, in no fixed order, possibly mid-parse. Both are ignored on inline classic scripts. Module scripts are deferred by default, `defer` does nothing to them, and `async` works on them even when inline.

## No attributes (the baseline)

For a classic script with `src` and neither attribute, "the script is fetched and evaluated immediately, blocking parsing until these are both complete" (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html). MDN adds that inline scripts without `type="module"` behave the same way: they run immediately, before parsing continues (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script).

## `defer` (classic scripts with `src`)

- **Parsing:** The script downloads in parallel with parsing and runs "when the page has finished parsing" (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html). It doesn't block the parser.
- **DOMContentLoaded:** It runs after the document is parsed but before `DOMContentLoaded` fires. Deferred scripts hold back `DOMContentLoaded` until they have loaded and run (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script). `document.readyState` is already `"interactive"` while they run (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/DOMContentLoaded_event).
- **Order:** Deferred scripts run in the order they appear in the document (MDN, same page). In the spec, a parser-inserted deferred script is added to the document's "list of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing", and the parser runs that list (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html).

## `async` (classic scripts with `src`)

- **Parsing:** The script downloads in parallel and runs "as soon as it is available (potentially before parsing completes)" (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html). The download doesn't block parsing, but running it can: an async script "can interrupt DOM building" if it arrives mid-parse (https://web.dev/articles/efficiently-load-third-party-javascript).
- **Order:** Each async script goes into a set (not a list) of "scripts that will execute as soon as possible" and runs when its own fetch completes (spec, same page). MDN puts it plainly: "You get no guarantee that scripts will run in any specific order." In practice, whichever finishes downloading first runs first.
- **DOMContentLoaded:** `DOMContentLoaded` does not wait for async scripts (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/DOMContentLoaded_event). An async script may run before or after it.
  - **Where sources disagree:** A note on that same MDN page says `DOMContentLoaded` fires "before the execution of scripts with async". That conflicts with the spec, which says async scripts may run before parsing finishes, and therefore before `DOMContentLoaded`. I follow the spec. Read MDN's note as describing a common case, not a rule.
- **Both attributes together:** `async` wins (MDN). The spec says adding `defer` alongside `async` exists only so that old browsers without `async` support fall back to deferring instead of blocking.

## Inline classic scripts

Both attributes do nothing when there is no `src`. MDN warns about this for each attribute. In the spec's processing steps, the async and defer branches apply only "If el's type is \"classic\" and el has a src attribute, or el's type is \"module\"". Inline classic scripts take the other path and normally run immediately, while the parser waits (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html).

## `type="module"`

- **Default:** Module scripts behave as if deferred. The module and its imports download in parallel and run when parsing finishes. "The defer attribute has no effect on module scripts" (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html). MDN agrees (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Modules). Like deferred classic scripts, they run before `DOMContentLoaded`.
- **With `async`:** The module and all its imports are fetched in parallel and the module runs as soon as everything is ready, possibly mid-parse, in no fixed order.
- **Inline modules:** The type check covers all module scripts, not just ones with `src`, so `async` applies to inline modules too. Even an inline module with no imports never runs synchronously, because the spec queues a task first.

## Summary

| Script | Blocks parsing? | Runs when | Order | Relation to DOMContentLoaded |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Classic, no attribute (external or inline) | Yes | Immediately | Document order | Before it |
| `defer` (external classic) | No | After parsing | Document order | Before; DOMContentLoaded waits for it |
| `async` (external classic) | Only while it runs | When downloaded | No guarantee | Before or after; not waited for |
| `defer`/`async` on inline classic | Yes (attributes ignored) | Immediately | Document order | Before it |
| `type="module"` | No | After parsing | Document order | Before; DOMContentLoaded waits for it |
| `type="module" async` (external or inline) | Only while it runs | When it and its imports are ready | No guarantee | Before or after |
